However, several Lean theorems (e.g., Thms 14-16) formalize trivial algebraic proxies while substantive physical premises remain external.

novelty.basis: Provides a disciplined quantitative synthesis adapting First-Law/Carnot floors, Hopfield A^2 ZPE scaling, Baffou spherical micro-hotspot no-go bounds, and an experimental OCR/CCCP/off-resonance matrix to 71-THz mitochondrial claims, rather than introducing new fundamental physical laws.

significance.basis: Establishes sharp falsification criteria and >72,900x single-organelle heating exclusions relevant to mid-IR bioenergetics preprints, though overall impact depends on an unrefereed bioRxiv preprint [7] and maintenance power figures imported from companion record [4].

reproducibility.basis: All model parameters, rational inputs, certificate metrics (C01-C16), and exact verification boundaries are clearly documented in the PDF. External Lean, Python, and JSON artifacts referenced in Section 3 were neither inspected nor executed during this PDF-only assessment.

summary: This manuscript presents a quantitative thermodynamic audit of claims that weak 71/87 THz mid-infrared irradiation (~10 mW/cm^2) elevates cellular ATP by ~10%. Inspecting the PDF equations, tables, and figures confirms the core derivations are accurate: stoichiometric conversion requires >= 1.765 71-THz photons per ATP (tightened by Carnot efficiency), the undiluted single-mode Hopfield A^2 ZPE shift is 7.456 meV (>2.92x the 2.546 meV Eyring shift) prior to 1/N dipole dilution, exact finite-difference Arrhenius kinetics require Delta T in (1.52, 1.54) K at E_a = 50 kJ/mol, and steady-state spherical conduction excludes single-mitochondrion hotspots by >72,900x (734.4 W/cm^2 at 1.53 K) while exposing >=2000x bulk dish amplification. The paper clearly distinguishes cellular [ATP] abundance from mitochondrial synthesis flux J_ATP and proposes a four-protocol experimental discriminator (water-matched off-resonance IR, oligomycin-sensitive OCR, CCCP uncoupling, irradiance sweep). Main limitations are that the classical Barato-Seifert TUR is satisfied by 10^3-10^4x at physiological respiration and does not constrain catalysis, the active coherent ratchet exclusion (>50x) imports P_maint ~ 4 nW unverified from companion work [4], driven VSC catalysis is treated phenomenologically without checking steady-state polariton occupancy at 10 mW/cm^2, and several Lean theorems formalize trivial algebraic proxies (Thms 14-16).
strengths: Exact, zero-linearization finite-difference Arrhenius identity (Eq. 4, Thm 6) and pi-free spherical micro-hotspot flux law (Eq. 5, Thm 8), rigorously excluding single-organelle heating at 10 mW/cm^2 by >72,900x (734.4 W/cm^2 at 1.53 K).

Rigorous rational Mercator alternating-series bracketing of ln(11/10) (11437/120000 < ln(11/10) < 143/1500) pinning |Delta E_a|_10% in (2.545, 2.547) meV, cleanly matched against the resonant Hopfield A^2 ZPE shift of (128/71) h*THz = 7.456 meV.

Essential bioenergetic distinction in Section 2.2 between cellular [ATP] abundance and steady-state mitochondrial synthesis flux J_ATP, yielding testable oligomycin-sensitive OCR (+10%, or >=+7.5% total mito OCR with <=25% leak) predictions.

Explicit, honest epistemic boundary in Section 3 separating kernel-checked integer/rational inequalities from analytical remainder bounds, continuum heat conduction, chemiosmotic kinetics, and unrefereed empirical claims from [7].
Clear, internally consistent tables and figures (C01-C16 and Table 3) providing a falsifiable four-protocol experimental matrix centered on off-resonance water-absorption-matched IR controls.
weaknesses: Classical Barato-Seifert TUR (Eq. 6, C13-C14) is non-binding for mitochondrial respiration: physiological entropy production (sigma*tau/k_B ~ 2x10^6 at tau = 1 s) exceeds the TUR floor by 10^3-10^4x, so it does not practically restrict classical catalysis.

Exclusion of active Regime II coherent ratchets (>50x power deficit vs 78.5 pW incident) relies on importing P_maint ~ 5x10^5 P_ATP^mito ~ 4 nW from companion record [4], which is neither re-derived nor independently checkable within this manuscript.

Driven resonant polaritonic catalysis (H_cat) is modeled phenomenologically via saturation Thm 20 without checking steady-state excited polariton occupancy per enzyme at 10 mW/cm^2 (~1.67x10^9 incident photons/s per mitochondrion, giving <<1 polariton at ps lifetimes).

Several Lean theorems formalize trivial algebraic proxies rather than substantive physics: Thm 14 assumes the TUR inequality as a premise, Thm 15 is a+b+c=d => a+b<=d, and Thm 16 models CCCP collapse via (11 k_cat)*0 = (10 k_cat)*0 = 0.

In Section 2.3 and Fig. 2b, 3D spherical scaling at L = 1 mm gives I_abs = 0.37 W/cm^2, which is still 37x above 10 mW/cm^2; achieving 10 mW/cm^2 bulk heating thus depends on unmodeled 1D planar substrate resistance or cm-scale illumination.
Table 1 row 12 encodes basal self-heating as 20000 < 4*314*6*5 without displaying the assumed basal power (<=20 fW) or scaling factor in the table statement itself.
potential_errors: Minor 0.01% rounding mismatch in Eq. (1): prose states h*71 THz = 293.63 meV (giving 518.2/293.63 = 1.7648), whereas the exact integer fraction 5182/2936 = 2591/1468 = 1.7650 uses 293.6 meV; both strictly exceed 1.76.

Thm 16 and Table 3 model forward ATP synthesis as proportional to Delta p (vanishing at Delta p = 0), whereas real F1Fo-ATP synthase reverses to hydrolyze ATP when Delta p drops below ~150-180 mV; accelerated k_cat under CCCP could increase ATP hydrolysis unless inhibited.

Fig. 2b labels the x-axis 'Heated region length scale L' while applying I_abs = 4*kappa_th*Delta T / L at L = 0.5 um (organelle radius, not 1 um diameter) and L = 1 mm, creating minor radius-versus-diameter ambiguity.
strong_novelty_candidates: Pi-free micro-hotspot flux exclusion law (I_micro = 4*kappa_th*Delta T / R) paired with exact finite-difference Arrhenius temperature shift, eliminating linearization error and geometric pi factors in organelle heating bounds.

Integrated four-mechanism bioenergetic discriminator matrix separating bulk heating, micro-hotspots, driven polaritonic catalysis, stoichiometric photon conversion, and demand/glycolytic [ATP] artifacts via water-matched IR and oligomycin-sensitive OCR.
